chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said:

I said to Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: May I perform some part of the rites while I am without wudu (ablution)? He said: Yes, except for the tawaf of the House, for indeed there is salat (prayer) in it.

key_terms.الْمَنَاسِكِ: the ritual acts and rites of hajj
key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: the Sacred House, meaning the Ka'bah
key_terms.صَلَاةً: salat (prayer), indicating a prayer-like legal status here
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: ritual ablution required for certain acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Can someone perform the rites of hajj without wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a person may take part in some of the hajj rites without wudu (ablution). The exception is tawaf around the Ka'bah, because it has the status of salat (prayer) in this ruling. It is a jurisprudential text concerning ritual purity during the manasik.
